This
revision petition

is preferred to question the correctness of the judgment dated 16th January, 2019 passed by learned IVth Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (E.C. Act), Aligarh in Criminal Appeal No. 282 of 2014 affirming the judgment dated 20th September, 2014 passed by learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 1, Aligarh holding the revision petitioner guilty for commission of an offence under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

entities.label: COURT

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In brief factual matrix of the case is that Sri Mohd. Yaseen Khan (PW-1), Food Inspector, Municipal Corporation, Aligarh filed a complaint under Section 7/16 before the Court of learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 1, Aligarh with assertion that in capacity of Food Inspector on 29th June, 1991, at about 9 a.m., he found that accused Bhagat Singh was selling butter.

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 1, Aligarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 450 gms of butter was purchased by the Food Inspector and that was divided in three equal parts.
One part was sent for its chemical examination by the public analyst, Lucknow.
As per the report No. 5191 given by the public analyst the samples of the butter sent to him were having less than 80% fat contained and as such, the same was adulterated.

On basis of the complaint aforesaid, the revision petitioner was tried and the contents of the application were supported by the ocular evidence given by Sri Mohd. Yaseen Khan (PW-1) and by relying upon certain documents, including the report given by the public analyst.
Sri Mohd. Yaseen Khan (PW-1) while getting his testimony examined stated that on 29th June, 1991, he was working as Food Inspector at Municipal Corporation, Aligarh.
At about 9 a.m., on the date aforesaid, he noticed that accused Bhagat Singh was carrying butter for sale.
After disclosing identity, he purchased 450 gms of butter and for that paid a sum of Rs. 20.25 to the accused Bhagat Singh.
The butter so purchased was divided in three equal parts and after necessary sampling and labelling the same was sent to the public chemical analyst.

A report dated 6th August,
1991 was received by the Food Inspector from the public chemical analyst and as per that the butter was adulterated.
The report then was forwarded to the Chief Medical Officer, Aligarh who granted sanction for prosecution vide the document Exhibit Ka-5.
On having necessary sanction complaint was filed vide Exhibit Ka-6 before the court competent and necessary information.

Suffice to state the statement aforesaid was recorded on 15th September, 1998 and on the same day this witness was subjected to cross examination by the counsel appearing on behalf of the accused.
The statement given by by PW-1 during his cross examination is as follows:-

sentences.text: "In the year 1991, I was posted in the area of Civil Lines.
I had collected the sample of (illegible) Bhagat (?) Singh from Dodpur (sic.).
I don't have good memory.
It is an incident happened 21 years ago.
I don't adequately remember (about it).
I remember only it that I had collected the sample.
Dodpur falls in the area of PS-Civil Lines.
At the time of collecting the samples, I had not taken any public witness.
The witnesses were from the staff.
It was a crowded place from where I had collected the sample.
The people were passing from there.
The milk of cow and that of buffalo is called mixed milk.
The butter made of the mixed milk is also called mixed (butter).
The mixed milk contains lesser fat than average.
I cannot state whether being adulterated the butter collected as sample was injurious to health or not.
The butter was found adulterated in the report of the Public Analyst.
My eye-sight is too weak to read.
I cannot state whether prior to it, I had seen Bhagat Singh carrying and selling the butter.
It is wrong to state that I had not collected the sample of the butter from Bhagat Singh and it is also wrong to state that the false proceeding had been conducted to implicate him."

The Trial Court by relying upon the statement given by Sri Mohd. Yaseen Khan and the report of public analyst Exhibit Ka-5 held the revision petitioner guilty and recorded his conviction and also awarded sentence to undergo six months imprisonment with a fine of Rs. 1000/-.
Appeal giving challenge to the order passed by the Trial Court came to be rejected by relying upon the same piece of evidence.

The submission of the revision petitioner is that to hold guilty for commission of an offence under Section 16(1)(a)(i) it is necessary to establish sale of prohibited article but, in the case in hand, there is no evidence to establish that the revision petitioner was having butter with him for the purpose of sale.
It is asserted that the revision petitioner defended himself with a plea that he was carrying butter for personal use and not for sale.
This fact as per the revision petitioner has not been taken into consideration by the Courts below.
I have looked into the documents passed by the Trial Court as well as by the Appellate Court.
On going through the record, it is apparent that throughout case of the revision petitioner was that he was carrying butter for his own use and not for sale.
It is also apparent from perusal of the record that the revision petitioner was not on any shop or at vending zone or at any permanent station for sale.
He was on his way and was stopped by the Food Inspector.
In such circumstance, the Courts below should have examined the fact as to whether the butter was carried by the accused revision petitioner for sale or for personal consumption.

There is no evidence on record to establish that the butter was carried by the revision petitioner for the purpose of sale except the statement given by Sri Mohd. Yaseen Khan (PW-1), who in cross examination stated that the entire incident is not in his memory being a stale one.
The documents on which the prosecution relied too does not disclose that the butter available with the revision petitioner was for sale.

In absence of the evidence in this regard is sufficient to arrive at a conclusion that no case is made out to hold the revision petitioner guilty for an offence under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
The Courts below have not taken into consideration this aspect of the matter.

sentences.text: them as such are not correct.
Accordingly, this revision petition is allowed.

The judgment dated 16th January, 2019 passed by learned IVth Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (E.C. Act), Aligarh in Criminal Appeal No. 282 of 2014 and the judgment dated 20th September, 2014 passed by learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 1, Aligarh are set aside.

entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 1, Aligarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The complaint filed by Sri Mohd. Yaseen Khan, the then Food Inspector, Nagar Nigam,
Aligarh fails.
Hence, the revision petitioner stands acquitted.
The revision petitioner on furnishing sureties and bonds has already been released, which are hereby discharged.
